name: net.apppage/app-data
title: AppPage.net - app websites & store data
description: App websites with privacy pages and app-ads.txt, plus Google Play & App Store app data.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Search Google Play or App Store apps by keyword (live results). Returns app ids, titles, developers, ratings and prices, each with an apppage_url page that has full details. When the user names an app ("Duolingo", "the Spotify app"), call this first to get its app_id, then use get_app, get_app_reviews, get_app_privacy or find_alternatives with that id.

query.description: Search keywords, e.g. "photo editor" or an app name.

store.description: Which store: google_play (Android, default) or app_store (iPhone/iPad).

country.description: Optional two-letter ISO 3166 store country code (e.g. US, GB, TR, DE). Defaults to US.

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Get details of one app. For Android pass the package name (e.g. com.whatsapp): developer with the contact email and website they publish on Google Play, category, rating and rating count, installs, price, in-app purchases, ads, version, size, required Android version, content rating, release and last-update dates, summary, description and recent changes. For iPhone/iPad pass the numeric App Store id (e.g. 310633997): the same kind of details plus required iOS version, star histogram and languages.

app_id.description: Android package name (e.g. com.whatsapp) or numeric App Store id (e.g. 310633997).

tools.name: find_alternatives
tools.description: List apps similar to a given app (the store's similar-apps list), compared by rating, price, installs (Android) and last update. Use for questions like "apps like X" or "alternatives to X".

app_id.description: Android package name (e.g. com.spotify.music) or numeric App Store id (e.g. 324684580).

tools.name: browse_category
tools.description: List Google Play or App Store top charts (live results): top free, top paid or top grossing apps, overall or in a category. Google Play categories look like game_puzzle or health_and_fitness; App Store categories look like games_puzzle or photo_and_video.

category.description: Optional category id (lowercase) for the chosen store. Omit for all apps.

chart.description: Which chart: top_free (default), top_paid or grossing.

store.description: Which store: google_play (Android, default) or app_store (iPhone/iPad).

country.description: Optional two-letter ISO 3166 store country code. Defaults to US.

tools.name: get_app_reviews
tools.description: Get user reviews of an app: star rating, date, text and app version; on Google Play also helpful votes and the developer's reply, on the App Store a review title. Read live from the store. For questions about what users say, like, dislike or complain about in an app, or about its 1-star / 5-star reviews (set stars). If the user gives an app name instead of an id, find the id with search_apps first.

app_id.description: Android package name (e.g. com.instagram.android) or numeric App Store id (e.g. 389801252).

sort.description: Order: most_relevant (default), newest or rating (rating is Google Play only).

country.description: Optional two-letter ISO 3166 store country code. Defaults to US.

stars.description: Optional: only reviews with this star rating (1-5), e.g. 1 for complaints.

tools.name: get_app_privacy
tools.description: Get an app's privacy information. Android: the Google Play data safety section (data shared with third parties, data collected and why, security practices, privacy policy link) and the Android permissions it requests, grouped by type. iPhone/iPad: Apple's App Privacy labels (data used to track you, data linked to you, data not linked to you) with data categories and purposes.

app_id.description: Android package name (e.g. com.whatsapp) or numeric App Store id (e.g. 310633997).

tools.name: get_developer_apps
tools.description: List the apps published by one developer. Google Play: by developer name as returned by other tools (e.g. "Wikimedia Foundation"). App Store: by developer_id from get_app or search_apps with store=app_store (a developer name also works; it is looked up by search).

developer.description: Developer name exactly as shown in the store, e.g. "Wikimedia Foundation".

developer_id.description: App Store only: numeric developer id, e.g. 310634000 (returned as developer_id by other tools).

store.description: Which store: google_play (Android, default) or app_store (iPhone/iPad).

country.description: Optional two-letter ISO 3166 store country code. Defaults to US.

tools.name: list_my_sites
tools.description: List the AppPage.net sites in your account: address, app, store, theme and which pages and app-ads.txt are filled in.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Details of one of your sites: its app, theme, page URLs, whether each page is filled in, and its app-ads.txt records.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: check_subdomain
tools.description: Check whether {subdomain}.apppage.net is free for a new site. 3-14 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.

subdomain.description: The address to check, e.g. "habitly" for habitly.apppage.net.

tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Create a website for a published app at {subdomain}.apppage.net, filled from its store listing (name, icon, screenshots, description, store buttons). Its privacy policy, terms, account deletion and support pages start empty: write them with set_page. Check the address with check_subdomain first.

app.description: Google Play: the package name (com.example.app) or its Play link. App Store: the numeric app id or its apps.apple.com link.

subdomain.description: The site address: {subdomain}.apppage.net. 3-14 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.

country.description: Optional two-letter store country the app is listed in, for App Store apps not in the US store.

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Change the design (theme) of one of your sites.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Read the current HTML of one of your site's pages: privacy_policy, terms, delete_account or support.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: generate_page
tools.description: Make one of your site's pages from AppPage.net's templates, the same ones as its privacy policy, terms, account deletion and support page generators: fixed, store-ready English text where each answer turns whole sections on or off. The app's name, developer, contact email (Google Play), website, platform, collected data types, ads, in-app purchases, version and the store's FAQ come from the store listing; your answers override them. Prefer this to writing a page yourself with set_page. Ask the user what the listing can't tell (SDKs, accounts, children, where they're based) before generating. save=false returns the page as Markdown without saving.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

answers.description: Optional answers; anything left out comes from the store listing or a safe default. privacy_policy: developer, email, website, countryName (where the developer is based), data (list of: account, phone, location, contacts, photos, audio, files, calendar, health, payments, messages, content, device, usage, diagnostics), services (list of SDK keys: firebase_analytics, crashlytics, sentry, mixpanel, amplitude, appsflyer, adjust, admob, applovin, unity_ads, meta_an, ironsource, liftoff, firebase_auth, google_signin, apple_signin, facebook_login, firebase_db, supabase, fcm, onesignal, play_billing, apple_iap, revenuecat, stripe, google_maps), account, deletionUrl, kids (directed at children), gdpr, ccpa, kvkk, retention (needed, device or account). terms: developer, email, website, countryName, minAge (any, 13, 16 or 18), price (free or paid), iap, subs, trial, virtual (in-app currency), ads, account, ugc (users post content), social (users talk to each other), ai (AI features), health. delete_account: developer, email, inApp + steps (list of in-app steps), byEmail, web + webUrl, deleted (list of: account, profile, content, messages, activity, location, health, device), keepPurchases + purchaseYears, keepLegal, keepBackups + backupDays, keepShared, keepStats, days (to delete), partial, subs. support: developer, email, website, reply (24h, 2d or 3d), purchases, subs, account, bugs, ipad, version, whatsNew, custom (list of {q, a} FAQ entries). Yes/no answers are true or false.

save.description: true (default) saves and publishes the page; false only returns it for review.

tools.name: set_page
tools.description: Replace one of your site's pages with new content: the privacy policy, terms and conditions, account deletion instructions (both stores ask for this page when an app has accounts) or support page with an FAQ. Write it in Markdown (default) or HTML; scripts, forms and event handlers are removed. Base it on what the app really does and collects (get_app_privacy shows its store privacy data), and include a contact email.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

content.description: The whole page, up to 100000 characters. It replaces the current one.

tools.name: set_app_ads_txt
tools.description: Write the app-ads.txt file served at https://{subdomain}.apppage.net/app-ads.txt, which ad networks (AdMob and others) check against the developer website in the store listing. One record per line: ad system domain, publisher account id, DIRECT or RESELLER, optional certification id, e.g. "google.com, pub-1234567890123456, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0". The lines are checked first; nothing is saved if any has an error. mode=append adds only the records that aren't there yet.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

mode.description: replace (default) the whole file, or append the new records.

tools.name: refresh_site_from_store
tools.description: Re-read the site's app from Google Play or the App Store now (name, icon, screenshots, description, what's new). Fields the store sends empty keep their current value. Once a minute per site.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: get_modules
tools.description: Which extras one of your sites has turned on (feedback board, bug reports, beta sign-up, promo codes, remote config, changelog, press kit, status page) with their URLs, its remote config, open status incidents, the latest changelog entries and its App Links files.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: set_module
tools.description: Turn one of your site's extras on or off: feedback (feature request board), reports (bug report form), beta (beta tester sign-up), promo (promo code page), remote_config (app-config.json for force updates, maintenance and notices), changelog, press (press kit) or status (status page). Their settings are kept.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

enabled.description: true to turn it on, false to turn it off.

tools.name: add_changelog_entry
tools.description: Add a release to your site's public changelog (and its RSS feed). Give version and notes, or from_store=true to add the store listing's current version and What's new. Turns the changelog on if it's off.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

notes.description: What changed, one item per line.

date.description: Release date yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out.

from_store.description: true to take the version and notes from the store listing instead.

tools.name: post_status_incident
tools.description: Post an incident on your site's status page, e.g. an outage or planned maintenance. Turns the status page on if it's off. Apps reading app-config.json can show it too.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: resolve_status_incident
tools.description: Mark an incident on your site's status page as resolved. get_modules lists the open incidents and their ids.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

message.description: Optional closing update, e.g. "Fixed; everything works again."

tools.name: set_remote_config
tools.description: Change the remote config your app reads from https://{site}/app-config.json: the lowest supported and latest versions per platform (apps below the lowest must update), the update message, maintenance mode and an in-app notice. Only the fields you pass change; pass "" to clear one. Turns remote config on.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

update_message.description: Shown when an update is needed.

maintenance.description: true puts the app in maintenance mode.

notice_url.description: Optional https link for the notice.

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Read what users sent through your site: feature requests on the feedback board (with votes and status) or bug reports (message, app version, OS and device; without the sender's email).

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

tools.name: set_app_links
tools.description: Write the files that let links to your site open your app: Apple's apple-app-site-association (Universal Links) and Android's assetlinks.json (App Links), served under https://{site}/.well-known/. Give ios_app_ids (TEAMID.bundle.id) and android_package with android_sha256 fingerprints, and they are built for you; or pass a whole file as apple_json / android_json. A platform you leave out keeps its file.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.

ios_app_ids.description: App IDs: your Apple team ID, a dot and the bundle id, e.g. ABCDE12345.com.example.app.

ios_paths.description: Paths that open the app; ["*"] (default) for all.

android_sha256.description: SHA-256 signing certificate fingerprints (Play Console › App integrity), AA:BB:... form.

apple_json.description: A whole apple-app-site-association file instead; "" removes it.

android_json.description: A whole assetlinks.json file instead; "" removes it.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Your AppPage.net plan (Free or Pro), what it includes and how much of today's API limit is used.

tools.name: set_custom_domain
tools.description: Serve one of your sites on your own domain, such as www.myapp.com (Pro). Returns the DNS record to add; the domain works once the record is in place and the certificate is issued. Call it again with the same domain to check progress.

site.description: Your site: its address ("habitly" for habitly.apppage.net) or id, as list_my_sites returns.
